sections.h2: What is Opelika, Alabama, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Opelika is the county seat of Lee County in east central Alabama and one of the two principal cities of the Auburn-Opelika metropolitan area. It sits at about 807 feet of elevation and covers roughly 62 square miles, with ZIP codes running from 36801 to 36804.

The Census Bureau counted 30,995 residents in 2020, a 17.1 percent gain over 2010, and a 2025 estimate of 35,765 appears in the city's reference listing. Auburn lies next door, and the metro area together with the Columbus, Georgia area forms a region of more than 500,000 people.

For sellers, that means Opelika buyers come from several directions. Some work in Opelika, some work in Auburn, and some commute toward Columbus.

sections.h2: How did Opelika start, and what does the railroad have to do with it?
sections.html:
Opelika was first settled in 1832 after the Treaty of Cusseta placed Creek lands under United States control, and the town kept its Creek name, which translates to "large swamp." It received a town charter on February 9, 1854, because the Montgomery and West Point Railroad had made it a shipping point for cotton.

The rail line shaped the downtown. The city nearly doubled in size between 1870 and 1900, and a rowdy period of saloons and factional fighting in 1882 led the state legislature to revoke the charter and appoint commissioners until 1899.

That history is useful when you sell an older house. Any house built in that period of growth is now well over a century old, and a buyer's inspector will look closely at structure, wiring and plumbing on one.

The 2020 census also found that 29.0 percent of Opelika households were one person living alone, and that 83.9 percent of residents lived in urban areas.

East Alabama Health is Opelika's largest employer, with more than 3,700 workers. The city's economic development figures say that since 2005 Opelika has seen more than $2.6 billion in new industry investment and expansions, creating over 4,700 additional jobs.

The Northeast Opelika Industrial Park is one of the city's industrial areas.

If you are selling a house in an area where an employer is expanding, it helps to know the commute distances and mention them to buyers. A cash buyer will do the same math before making an offer.

Opelika has a mayor and council government, with a mayor elected at large for a four year term and a five member city council. The mayor holds full executive power and can appoint and dismiss department heads, which makes the mayor's office the main contact for city policy questions.

In 2007 the council designated Opelika a City of Character, a program built around 49 character traits. For a seller the practical matter is that permits, code questions and utility accounts go through city departments, so call the city before you assume a rule applies or does not apply to your house.

sections.h2: What is the culture of Opelika like?
sections.html:
Opelika has a small but active arts and media profile. The Opelika Community Theatre was founded in 2015, the film Norma Rae was shot in the city in 1979, and the Opelika-Auburn News is the local paper. The city is part of the Columbus, Georgia television market.

These details help describe the area to a relocating buyer, though they rarely change the value of a single house. What affects value more is condition, location and price.

sections.h2: What parks and public facilities does Opelika have?
sections.html:
Opelika has invested heavily in public amenities over the past two decades, which shapes how neighborhoods are described to buyers:

  • Spring Villa Park, a 350 acre park with picnic areas, nature trails, two disc golf courses and camping, plus an antebellum house on the National Register of Historic Places.
  • The Opelika SportsPlex and Aquatics Center, a $32 million facility built in 2009.
  • The Opelika Pickleball Facility, opened in 2019 with 24 regulation courts.
  • The Opelika Public Library, a $12 million building that opened in 2021 with a 250 person auditorium.
  • The RTJ Golf Trail at Grand National, part of the Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail.

Homes near these facilities usually mention them in listings, and a house within a short drive of a park or sportsplex has an easy selling point to highlight.

Opelika City Schools is the public system and runs nine schools: three primary schools for kindergarten through grade 2, three intermediate schools for grades 3 to 5, one sixth grade school, one middle school for grades 7 and 8, and Opelika High School for grades 9 to 12.

Because the grades are split across several buildings, a seller who can name the assigned schools for an address answers one of the first questions a family asks.

Southern Union State Community College also has a campus in Opelika, and Auburn University is a short drive away.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit work in Opelika?
sections.html:
Opelika is served by Interstate 85, US 29, US 280 and US 431, and by Alabama State Routes 14 and 51. Lee-Russell Public Transit provides dial-a-ride service through the city and region, and there has been no passenger rail since the Illinois Central's City of Miami made its last run in 1971.

With a city that spans about 62 square miles, drive time to the interstate varies a lot from one address to another, so state the distance when you list or discuss the house.

sections.h2: What do Opelika sellers pay at closing and when are taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama collects a deed recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, paid before the probate judge records the deed, according to Alabama Code section 40-22-1. For a $100,000 sale, the formula gives $100.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. Lee County offices keep the parcel records, so ask them for current balances before choosing a closing date.

The tax year runs on that October cycle, so a sale in the fall can involve a bill that has just come due. Make sure the closing statement shows who covers it.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit an Opelika house?
sections.html:
A cash offer suits sellers who need certainty more than a long listing period. Common Opelika situations include:

  • An older house near downtown that needs electrical, plumbing or roof work.
  • An inherited property that the family wants to close out.
  • A rental with deferred maintenance or a tenant who is not paying.
  • A house the owner must sell before a move to or from the Auburn or Columbus area.

Before you accept any offer, compare it with what a listing could realistically net after repairs, agent fees and the months a house may sit. The Auburn-Opelika metro area has about 174,000 residents, so the pool of local buyers is not unlimited, and a house that needs work can take a while to find the right one. We buy Opelika houses as they stand and you can decline any offer.

faqs.a: Opelika is in Lee County, Alabama, and it is the county seat.

faqs.q: How many people live in Opelika?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 30,995 residents, and the 2025 estimate cited for the city is 35,765.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Opelika?
faqs.a: The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Opelika?
faqs.a: East Alabama Health is the largest employer, with more than 3,700 employees, according to the city's economic development figures.

faqs.q: Where does the name Opelika come from?
faqs.a: It comes from the Creek words opilwa, meaning swamp, and lako, meaning big, and is usually translated as large swamp.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Opelika house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, so repairs and cleaning are not required before closing.
